stories.title: Invasive heart procedures offer no long-term survival edge
stories.summary: Patients with stable heart disease and abnormal stress tests who undergo early invasive procedures do not live longer than those treated with drugs and lifestyle changes alone, according to an international study. The invasive approach provides no survival advantage over standard medical management.

stories.title: Statin discontinuation deemed safe for older adults
stories.summary: Adults aged 70 and older who take statins to prevent cardiovascular disease but have not experienced a heart attack or stroke may safely discontinue the medication. These findings were presented as preliminary late-breaking science at a recent medical meeting.

stories.title: Lupus patients show low response to treatment escalation
stories.summary: Fewer than one-quarter of patients with systemic lupus erythematosus reach major clinical response criteria after escalating treatment, according to a study in The Lancet Rheumatology. Black patients were found to be less likely to meet these response criteria than white patients.

stories.title: Intensive blood pressure therapy fails to cut diabetes heart risks
stories.summary: Intensive treatment to lower systolic blood pressure below 120 mm Hg in adults with type 2 diabetes did not significantly reduce the incidence of cardiovascular death, stroke, or heart attack. The strategy failed to provide additional protection against major cardiovascular events.

stories.title: Statin combinations yield similar heart outcomes to monotherapy
stories.summary: Adults with heart or blood vessel disease who started treatment with a statin alone had heart attack and stroke rates similar to those who combined a statin with ezetimibe. The addition of the nonstatin medication did not change three-year outcomes.

stories.title: Doxycycline use in early pregnancy linked to loss
stories.summary: A retrospective study found that using doxycycline to treat respiratory infections or acne during early pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of pregnancy loss. The findings highlight potential risks for women of childbearing age who frequently use the antibiotic.

stories.title: New surface coating could help implants bond better with bone in people with diabetes
stories.summary: 🛡️ Just a quick check We’re checking your connection to prevent automated abuse Flinders University researchers are launching an innovative surface-engineering technology that could help to raise the performance of implantable medical devices in people with diabetes and other metabolic diseases.

stories.title: Health Ministry updates microbial monitoring rules
stories.summary: The Health and Family Welfare Ministry proposed amendments to align microbial monitoring in sterile manufacturing with World Health Organization guidelines. Any microbial growth detected in critical Grade A zones will now trigger a formal investigation under the revised regulatory standards.

stories.title: Chennai hospitals report dozens of Diwali eye injuries
stories.summary: Ophthalmologists in Chennai treated dozens of cracker-related eye injuries over the Deepavali weekend. The Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital reported approximately 50 cases, with 10 patients requiring admission. Doctors continue to reiterate the need for protective measures.

stories.title: AIIMS Delhi treats 42 burn cases following Diwali
stories.summary: AIIMS Delhi recorded 42 burn injury patients during the Diwali period, including 11 who were seriously hurt. Four patients were admitted to the intensive care unit and five have undergone surgery. Children accounted for a significant share of the total cases.

stories.title: Health Ministry proposes immediate licence suspension for substandard drugs
stories.summary: The Health Ministry has proposed a rule to suspend the licences of manufacturers producing substandard drugs. Suspensions would remain in place until the licence holder completes a root cause analysis and implements corrective actions to the satisfaction of the licensing authority.

stories.title: Delhi air quality monitoring stations go offline during peak pollution
stories.summary: Delhi recorded its most polluted Diwali in five years, but official figures were incomplete as several monitoring stations went offline during peak firecracker use. Private agencies reported hazardous levels while official data remained limited. The air quality monitoring exercise is now facing questions regarding its overall reliability.

stories.title: Community environments drive diabetes care disparities in India
stories.summary: A nationwide investigation found that community-level environments account for the largest proportion of geographic variation in diabetes care, exceeding district or state-level differences. While awareness and treatment rates are moderate, effective blood sugar management remains low. Disparities are rooted in local settings rather than broader administrative borders.

stories.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed vehicular emissions a major contributor to air pollution in Delhi-NCR and said immediate, medium- and long-term measures were needed to curb the rising air quality index. stories.title: Anti-cancer drug prices capped to save consumers billions
stories.summary: Revised maximum retail prices for 1,364 anti-cancer formulations took effect on November 9, 2026. The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority capped trade margins on 137 drugs following expert committee recommendations. The move is projected to save consumers 3,540 crore rupees annually across 85 pharmaceutical companies.

stories.title: Air pollution linked to over 2 million deaths in India
stories.summary: More than 20 lakh deaths in India were attributable to air pollution in 2023, according to a report by FICCI and EY. The findings suggest the country’s air quality should be treated as a public health emergency. Industry bodies are now seeking a health-led clean air policy.

stories.title: FDA investigates growing Salmonella Javiana outbreak
stories.summary: Federal health officials are investigating a Salmonella Javiana outbreak that has sickened at least 65 people across the United States. The FDA has not identified a specific food source, brand, or distributor associated with the illnesses. Investigators are currently tracing products through the supply chain.

stories.title: Mpox outbreak reported in Anchorage
stories.summary: State health officials in Alaska have reported four cases of mpox in Anchorage, the highest annual count since 2022. None of the patients reported recent travel outside the state. The viral disease is spread through close contact and is currently being monitored by the Department of Health.

stories.title: Gaza floods destroy thousands of tents
stories.summary: A rainstorm flooded approximately 70,000 tents housing displaced Palestinians in Gaza, prompting civil defence authorities to declare a state of maximum emergency. Authorities have requested international pressure to allow the entry of specialised rescue equipment and emergency shelter supplies as winter conditions worsen in the camps.

stories.title: Train collision in Egypt kills seven
stories.summary: A train traveling from Giza to Fayoum struck the rear of another train heading to Aswan, killing seven people and injuring 112. The collision occurred in the Al-Ayyat area. Several carriages derailed during the incident, which is currently being handled by the Egyptian railway authority.

stories.title: Four killed in Gaza after embankment collapse
stories.summary: Three children and one woman died when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in central Gaza following heavy rain. Five other people were rescued from the site. The Civil Defence service has described the incident as a humanitarian tragedy requiring urgent action to provide safe shelter.

stories.title: Gaza health ministry reports mass displacement from floods
stories.summary: Weekend flooding has left 350,000 displaced Palestinians sleeping in the open, according to the Gaza Health Ministry. Director-General Munir al-Bursh issued an urgent appeal for shelter supplies and the opening of crossings, warning that children face mortal danger as winter storms continue to batter the enclave.

stories.title: Hantavirus outbreak suspected on cruise ship
stories.summary: Three people have died and four others are ill following a suspected hantavirus outbreak aboard the MV Hondius. The World Health Organization confirmed two laboratory cases and five suspected cases among the 149 people on board. Investigations and laboratory testing are currently ongoing off the coast of Cape Verde.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo reaches record scale
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is experiencing the largest Ebola outbreak in its history, with 10,668 confirmed cases and 5,198 deaths recorded as of November 3, 2026. Transmission remains active in 51 health zones. The WHO reported 964 new cases since late October.

stories.title: Caregiver support startup raises 3.5 million dollars
stories.summary: Avanlee Care raised 3.5 million dollars in seed funding to support family caregivers. The startup integrates with Medicare Advantage plans to help manage medications, appointments, and grocery shopping. It provides wellness tools for caregivers and maintains partnerships with national retailers and the Mark Cuban Cost Plus Drug Company.

stories.title: Digital health firms pivot to cardiometabolic health
stories.summary: Executives at the INVEST Digital Health conference say their strategy for managing GLP-1 patients is shifting beyond weight loss to cardiometabolic health. Noom vice president Alexander Fabry told the audience that patients are not seeking a drug, but health. The industry is now attempting to provide the latter.

stories.title: Digital tools show modest gains in COPD activity
stories.summary: A meta-analysis of 26 randomized controlled trials found that digital health interventions increased daily physical activity in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Users took an average of 684.80 more steps per day than control groups. The study was published in BMC Pulmonary Medicine.

stories.title: Primary care digital integration remains fragmented
stories.summary: A systematic review of digital health technologies in primary care found that evidence regarding operational efficiency remains fragmented. Researchers synthesized data on integrated tools including artificial intelligence and electronic health records. The study highlights the current state of digital transformation in routine service management.

stories.title: Researchers propose smart televisions for women's health
stories.summary: Researchers from The University of Texas suggest smart televisions could serve as an untapped platform for digital health interventions. Femtech has historically relied on smartphone applications, while televisions remain viewed as passive devices. The perspective was published in Frontiers in Global Women’s Health.

stories.title: Union Health Ministry reviews digital mission progress
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry reviewed the implementation of the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and the Jan Arogya Yojana. Discussions focused on expanding healthcare coverage and strengthening digital infrastructure. The review featured a demonstration of the National Health Authority's ambient AI-enabled voice scribe.

stories.title: Gaza health officials report displacement crisis
stories.summary: Gaza Health Ministry Director-General Munir al-Bursh reported that flooding has left 350,000 displaced Palestinians without shelter. Al-Bursh stated that thousands of tents are waiting at crossings, but are currently being denied entry. The ministry is calling for urgent supplies to protect children at displacement sites.

stories.title: Centre reviews Ayushman Bharat digital initiatives
stories.summary: The Centre held a two-day meeting in Kolkata to review the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission and the Jan Arogya Yojana. The focus included healthcare quality, digital services, and AI integration. The National Health Authority is overseeing efforts to strengthen financial protection and expand digital health services.

stories.title: Study explores link between creativity and mental health
stories.summary: Researchers from the Max Planck Institute and Karolinska Institutet published a study in Molecular Psychiatry examining the relationship between creativity and mental health. The research aims to provide empirical evidence for the historical belief that high levels of creativity are often paired with mental health challenges.

stories.title: Psychedelic use linked to anxiety relief in younger adults
stories.summary: A survey of 1,088 adults published in Scientific Reports found that psychedelic use is associated with lower anxiety and depression only in younger age groups. The link weakened as participant age increased and was absent among older demographics. The study follows growing interest in psychedelic-assisted psychiatric treatments.

stories.title: Basic support linked to lower distress in refugees
stories.summary: A survey of refugees in Ugandan settlements found that those receiving food or water support reported lower odds of depression and anxiety. The study highlights the impact of humanitarian aid on mental health in a region that has historically seen limited research on displaced populations.

stories.title: Self-compassion and emotional malleability in youth
stories.summary: A longitudinal study of 719 secondary school students suggests that believing negative emotions can change links self-compassion to better mental health. Published in Child and Adolescent Psychiatry and Mental Health, the research explores how a self-compassionate mindset may influence well-being over time.

stories.title: Depression linked to lower employment in Indian adults
stories.summary: A study of 27,092 Indian adults aged 45 to 60 years found that depression is associated with a lower likelihood of employment. Researchers used the Composite International Diagnostic Interview to assess symptoms. The data indicates that as depressive symptoms increase, the likelihood of working falls.

stories.title: Youth struggle to interpret public health surveys
stories.summary: A qualitative study of the Swedish National Public Health Survey found that young people struggle to interpret questions regarding psychological distress. The findings suggest that survey responses may reflect individual interpretations rather than the underlying conditions the questions intend to measure.

stories.title: Study links daily step count to cognitive performance
stories.summary: A 14-year study suggests that daily step counts are linked to better focus and decision-making. While physical benefits of walking are well-documented, the research indicates that movement throughout the day may also influence how well the brain functions during complex tasks.

stories.title: Aerobic fitness in youth linked to adult mental health
stories.summary: A study of over 1,000 Australians published in the Journal of Affective Disorders suggests that higher aerobic fitness in childhood is linked to a lower risk of clinical depression by middle age. Muscular strength showed much weaker ties to adult mental health outcomes.

stories.title: Review links ageing attitudes to mental health
stories.summary: A systematic review published in the European Journal of Ageing synthesized evidence on how internalised views of ageing affect mental health. The study assessed how negative age stereotypes may serve as a vulnerability factor for depression and anxiety in later life.

stories.title: Distressed Israeli users turn to AI for support
stories.summary: A study from Tel Hai University found that nearly half of Israeli users experiencing severe psychological distress turn to generative AI for support. Researchers suggest the technology may act as a digital bandage that potentially deepens isolation while promising comfort.

research.title: A little-known protein could be a major culprit in type 2 diabetes
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that a buildup of a protein called Miro1 may be a hidden driver of insulin resistance in Type 2 diabetes, with preclinical experiments showing that removing it restores the muscles’ response to insulin. Exercise was also found to lower Miro1 levels in people with diabetes.

research.title: A simple supplement may help clear brain fog after cancer
research.summary: A surprising new study from UCLA suggests that a naturally occurring molecule could help breast cancer survivors overcome the frustrating brain fog and exhaustion that can linger long after treatment ends. Researchers found that women taking an oxaloacetate supplement for eight weeks experienced substantial improvements in memory, concentration.

research.title: An ulcerative colitis taxonomy defined by individual patient-reported response trajectories
research.summary: Nature Medicine, Published online: 09 November 2026, doi:10.1038/s41591-026-04741-8 An analysis of patient-reported trajectories of response to vedolizumab in ulcerative colitis defines disease endotypes and identifies vascular inflammation as a potential resistance mechanism.

research.title: Common osteoporosis drugs linked to 24% lower dementia risk in major study
research.summary: A massive study of more than 120,000 older adults suggests that common osteoporosis drugs may reduce the risk of Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias by up to 24%. The surprising findings raise the possibility that medications already used to strengthen bones could also help protect the aging brain.

research.title: Common supplement could help fight psoriasis, scientists discover
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that pantethine, a readily available vitamin B5 derivative, can calm overactive immune cells and may help fight psoriasis. The supplement prevented psoriasis in mice and showed promising results in a small human trial, revealing an unexpected connection between cholesterol and autoimmune inflammation.

research.title: Scientists discover a surprising link between acorns and lyme disease
research.summary: After more than 35 years of research, scientists have uncovered surprising clues about what really drives Lyme disease risk. Contrary to longstanding assumptions, deer populations appear less important than mice, which can fuel a 40% increase in tick numbers the following year. Even acorn production can predict tick.
